2. Plaintiffs claimed that from before the settlement operation, the villagers of Gandina Hindu Community established a temple and set up the image of Sree Sree Shashan Kalimata and had been performing religious rites. In the settlement operation, the lands were recorded in the name of ex-landlord but in the remark column the "Kodaldoha Kalibari by the Hindu community" was shown as possessor. Subsequently, with a view to remove the complication that might arise in future, Abinash Chandra Ghosh and others executed a deed of Endowment on 1st September, 1947 in favour of the Sree Sree Shashan Kalimata and the local Hindu community had been performing religious rites thereon. The villagers appointed the defendant No.1 as the Shebait for the management of the properties of the deity and to perform other religious rites. During the last settlement operation, the suit lands were recorded in the name of Abinash Chandra Ghosh and others and consequent upon which the Shebait instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 338 of 1968 under section 143 (a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The said case was allowed and the civil Court directed the Revenue Authority to record the suit lands in the name of the deity. The Shebait was not performing the religious rites regularly and he did not maintain the accounts of the deity's property and misappropriated the entire usufructs of the property. Subsequently, the plaintiffs' appointed one Santosh Kumar Chakraborty as pujari of the deity for performing religious rites. Subsequently, the defendant No. 1 removed the image of the deity from the suit lands and converted the suit property as his personal property. 

 3. Defendant No.1, in his written statement claimed for the dismissal of the suit by raising various pleas. His first point is that the plaintiffs have no locus standi to institute the suit as they are believor of worshipping Vishnu, who are not entitled to offer Shashan Kalipuja not to speak of appointing a Sheba it of the deity. The second point raised by the defendant is that there is no legal evidence about mismanagement and/or misappropriation of the deity's property. The third point is that since the plaintiffs and other villagers are not entitled to perform Kali puja, the suit is barred under section 15 of the Religious Endowment Act, 1863. The last point agitated by the defendant is that the suit property not being the trust property of the deity, the suit, in accordance with section 92, is not legally maintainable. 

 8. Mr Mir Mahfuzur Rahman, learned Advocate, has reiterated the defendant's plea taken in the written statement and submits that the plaintiffs, being members of Sudra and Baishnab community, have no right to perform the Kalipuja; they have no right to institute the suit to remove the hereditary Shebait, who is the Brahman of Kaishta Sect. Mr Rahman argues that the deed of endowment clearly recites that the deity has been established for performing religious rites by the Kaishta sect. In this connection the learned Advocate, has taken us to a book written by Pundit Shri Syama Charan Bhattacharya regarding the procedure of performing Sree Kalipuja. The learned Advocate has placed page 117 of the said scripture wherein the procedure of medi- tation ofKalimata has been narrated. By referring to this scripture, the learned Advocate is trying to make out a case that the non believers of Shashan Kalimata have restrictions to eat meat and that the plaintiffs, being believers of worshipping Vishnu, are not touching meat and therefore, they are not entitled to perform religious rites of Shashan Kalimata. The learned Advocate has also taken us to a book "Guru Bhakti Tatta Sudha" written by Shri Jodumondan Goswami and by referring pages 136, 142 and 143, the learned Advocate wants to convince us that the Baishnaba sects are performing the seba puja of Sree Krishna, who are not legally entitled to perform Shashan Kalimata puja. The learned Advocate has also taken us to Rigved wherein the different sects of Hindu Community and their mode of performing different types of seba puja have been narrated. The substance of the argument of the learned Advocate by bringing an analogy from these religious books is that the plaintiffs have no right or locus standi to interfere with the internal management of the properties of Shashan Kalimata as they are not believers of the image of the Shashan Kalimata. 

 13. A religious endowment which is known as Debuttor and which arises on dedication or gift of property to an idol, a Debuttor is managed and administered and it is in an ideal sense that the dedicated property vests in an idol and in the nature of things the possession and management of it is entrusted to some person as Shebait. He is the person entitled to speak on behalf of the deity on earth and is endowed with authority to deal with all its temporal affairs. In a Hindu religious endowment, the entire owner- ship of the dedicated property vests in the trustee, who holds it for the benefit of Cestui Que trust. The entire ownership of the dedicated property is transferred to the deity. It is an admitted fact that the plaintiff is the Shebait of the deity. Now the question iswhat is the status of the Shebait of a public debuttor property. It has been observed by the judicial committee in Prosonna Kumari Debya vs Golap Chand Baboo, (1875) LR 2 IA 145 "that the person so entrusted must, of necessity, be empowered to do whatever may be required for the service of the idol and for the benefit and preservation of each property, at least as great as the manager of an infant heir. If these were not so, the estate of the idol might be destroyed or wasted, and its worship discontinued for want of necessary funds to preserve and maintain them." 

 14. BK Mukharjea also told that the exact position of a Shebait cannot be said to be altogether beyond the range of controversy, though much of the earlier theories has now been discarded. The relation of a Shebait in regard to the debuttor property is not that of a trustee to trust property under the English law. In English Law, the legal estate in the trust property vests in the trustee who holds it for the benefit of the Cestui Que trust. In a Hindu religious endowment, the entire ownership of the dedicated property is transferred to the deity or institution itself as a juristic person and the Shebait or Mahant is a mere Manager. In Vidyavarathi vs Balu Sami, LR 48IA 302 the judicial committee observed. "A trust in the sense in which the expression is used in English Law, is unknown in the Hindu system pure and simple. Hindu Piety found expression in gifts to idols and images consecrated and installed in temples, to religious institution of every count, and for all purposes considered meritorious in the Hindu social and religious system. Under the Hindu law, the image of a deity of the Hindu Pantheon is a juristic entity, vested in the capacity of receiving gifts and holding property. Religious institutions known under different names are regarded as possessing the same juristic capacity and gifts are made to their committee". Now the question is, whether an interested person or a worshipper can maintain a suit for protecting the deity's property and whether he can remove the Shebait by a suit. 

 18. It is contended that in view of the admission of PW 1 that he is a believer of Vishnu and therefore, he cannot perform Shashan Kalipuja. PW 1 however, stated in course of cross-examination that his mother was cremated at the suit cremation ground. Mr Mir Mahfuzur Rahman, argues that this cremation of the PW 1 's mother in the suit cremation ground will not confer him any right to perform Shashan Kalipuja since he is not the believer of the said rites. 

 19. The Nitisara tells us "neither through colour, nor through ancestors can the spirit worthy of a Brahman be generated." Thus, according to it, caste division should not be by birth, but by capacity. Again, it says" in making official appointments work, character, and merit were to be regarded neither caste nor the family." "public opinion is more powerful than the king as the rope made of many fibres is strong enough to drag a lion." A man can rise by capacity and merit. But how is he to acquire the capacity and merit? Jawaharlal Nehru in Glimpses of World History stated: "Probably the writer of Nitisara did not consider the large number of Shudra workers as entitled to give opinion. They are hardly counted. Public opinion was perhaps, just the opinion of the upper and ruling classes." "The books however, help us to realise what the ideology or the ideas of the people were at the time, even though they may not have practised them wholly. A more frequent method of rising in the social scale was for a whole sub-caste to go up a step. New tribes were often absorbed into Hinduism at the bottom, slowly they worked themselves up." "Thus, caste was a group system based on service and functions. It was meant to be an all-inclusive order without any common dogma and allowing the fullest latitude to each group. Within its wide fold there was monogamy, polygamy and celibacy; they are all tolerated, just as other customs, beliefs and practices were tolerated. Life was to be maintained at all levels. No minority need submit to a majority, for it could always form a separate autonomous group, the only test being; it is a distinctive group large enough to function as such. Between two groups there could be any amount of variation of race, religion, colour, culture and intellectual development." 

 "In a case of this description, if the purchase was allowed, precisely the same mischiefs would result as have been apprehended by eminent judges in cases of purchases of trust properties by trustees for sale. Indeed, the mischief might be of a more aggravated character, less likely to be discovered than rectified, as, unless the Shebait was removed, it might be impossible to determine the impropriety of the transaction and the injury inflicted thereby on the debuttor estate. If the contrary view prevailed, it is not inconceivable that an unscrupulous Shebait, anxious to seize a particular portion of the debuttor estate for his personal use, might, notwithstanding ample funds at his disposal, be encouraged to borrow money in the character of Shebait, allow a decree to be passed against him, acquiesce in the consequent execution sale, and ultimately, purchase the property in his private capacity." 

 30. DW 2 also admitted that there was existence of Mondir in the suit lands. In course of cross-examination, he stated that he did not see the performing Kalipuja by the defendant-appellant after the liberation of Bangladesh and that the defendant whimsically maintains the income and expenditure of the deity's property. DW 3, in course of cross-examination, also admitted that there is no existence of Kali-Mondir in the suit lands and that he did not see any Mondir in the suit lands for the last about 28 years. He further admitted that the defendant sometimes performed seba puja of the Kalimata by him and sometimes through other thakurs. DW 5 also admitted in course of cross- examination that there is no existence of any Mondir. There. is therefore, admitted evidence on record that there was a Mondir and the image of the Kalimata in the suit land and the defendant- appellant had removed the Mondir and the image of the idol. The purpose for which the lands were endowed were not utilised and the properties were used for personal purpose of the defendant. The defendant-appellant has got the lands recorded in his own name. These facts manifestly proved that the defendant-appellant has mismanaged and misappropriated the property of the deity.
